name: WHO Reporting System for Lymph Node, Spleen and Thymus Cytopathology
edition: IAC-IARC-WHO cytopathology reporting systems series, 1st ed., vol. 3 (2024)
specimen: FNAB of lymph node, spleen, thymus/mediastinum

adequacy.title: Adequacy
items: Representative material; dedicated passes for flow cytometry and cell block.

categories.name: Inadequate / Insufficient / Non-diagnostic

rom.source: WHO Reporting System (IAC-IARC), 1st ed – book chapter text – pooled meta-analysis cited

categories.management: Correlate with clinical and imaging data rather than reflexly repeating. Low suspicion → follow-up; clear suspicion → repeat FNAB (image guidance, ROSE, ancillary passes), core or excision. Never report as negative; audit rates. [WHO book, paraphrased]
criteria: Scant lymphoid cells, blood, necrosis only.

diagnoses.name: Non-diagnostic
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO LN/Spleen/Thymus System – Inadequate/Insufficient/Non-diagnostic

categories.name: Benign

rom.source: WHO Reporting System (IAC-IARC), 1st ed – book chapter text – pooled meta-analysis cited

categories.management: Usually conservative clinical/imaging/laboratory follow-up. Excision if discordant. Repeat FNAB with flow, core or excision if the node changes, B symptoms appear, or a hard node >20 mm persists/enlarges; repeat under ultrasound if first FNA was palpation-guided. [WHO book, paraphrased]
criteria: Polymorphous reactive lymphoid population; granulomatous lymphadenitis; abscess; thymoma-free benign thymic tissue; splenic reactive/haemangioma.

diagnoses.name: Reactive lymphoid hyperplasia
diagnoses.final: Benign (WHO LN/Spleen/Thymus System). Reactive lymphoid hyperplasia.
diagnoses.comment: Clinical correlation and ancillary studies recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO LN/Spleen/Thymus System – Benign

categories.name: Atypical

rom.source: WHO Reporting System (IAC-IARC), 1st ed – book chapter text – pooled meta-analysis cited

categories.management: Review clinical/imaging, seek colleague review and MDT; ancillary tests if material allows (scant cell blocks are a caution); often repeat FNAB with ROSE triage ± core biopsy. [WHO book, paraphrased]
criteria: Lymphoid population with partial monotony; atypical cells few.

diagnoses.name: Atypical lymphoid cells
diagnoses.final: Atypical (WHO LN/Spleen/Thymus System). Atypical lymphoid cells.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO LN/Spleen/Thymus System – Atypical

categories.name: Suspicious

rom.source: WHO Reporting System (IAC-IARC), 1st ed – book chapter text – pooled meta-analysis cited

categories.management: Integrate clinical, imaging and flow data (report may be issued with ancillary pending). Suspected metastasis → core or repeat FNAB with cell block/ICC. Suspected lymphoma → core biopsy with flow ± ICC/NGS. [WHO book, paraphrased]
criteria: Suspicious for lymphoma or metastasis, insufficient.

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for lymphoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious (WHO LN/Spleen/Thymus System). Suspicious for lymphoma.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO LN/Spleen/Thymus System – Suspicious

diagnoses.name: Suspicious for metastatic carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Suspicious (WHO LN/Spleen/Thymus System). Suspicious for metastatic carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Clinical correlation and ancillary studies recommended.
diagnoses.cat: Diagnostic category: WHO LN/Spleen/Thymus System – Suspicious

categories.name: Malignant

rom.source: WHO Reporting System (IAC-IARC), 1st ed – book chapter text

categories.management: Ancillary testing for specific diagnosis/primary site. Lymphoma generally needs core and often excision (recommended for Hodgkin, T-cell lymphoma and follicular grading), though practice varies. [WHO book, paraphrased]
criteria: Metastatic carcinoma/melanoma; high-grade lymphoma; Hodgkin lymphoma; thymoma/thymic carcinoma.

diagnoses.name: Metastatic squamous cell carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Malignant (WHO LN/Spleen/Thymus System). Metastatic squamous cell carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Clinical correlation and ancillary studies recommended.
